content.comment_body: I realized I missed that the device must be in run mode to access the webserver. Sorry [user_name], I overlooked that. Now I need to add a Summer/Winter switch to disable output Q3 in Winter mode and enable it in Summer. I also must implement a function to stop a pump if pipe flow is insufficient; the flow meter sends an analog signal if the flow is out of range. Additionally, I want a function for the water meter, which uses M-bus pulses to calculate added water—displaying daily and monthly totals. I don't think my abilities with [product_name] are enough for this. Are you interested in helping me with these functions?
The [product_name] cannot communicate directly with M-Bus. Currently, it only supports communication via Ethernet TCP/IP or Modbus TCP/IP using the [protocol_name] protocol.
Is there a way to convert the M-bus signal? This is not a priority function, but the others are.
I'm not sure. In addition to converting the bus, the water meter must support the [protocol_name] protocol.
Okay, I'll look into this and search for a converter. Could you help me with the other functions? I feel it's beyond my current skills with [product_name].

There's no built-in method in [product_name] to programmatically check for summer or winter times. You can only use a yearly timer together with the weekly timer, but each year you need to manually enter the summer and winter dates.
I meant a physical switch connected to the device, like on/off. Sorry if my explanation wasn't clear.
Do you mean a signal from an external digital input to the [product_name]? If so, what's preventing you from switching output Q3 on and off?

Yes, I mean an external digital input. I tried to set it up, but I can't get it to work (I'm new to this) and need help. When the input is active (1), it should disable output Q3; when inactive (0), Q3 should be enabled. Even if the temperature drops, Q3 should stay disabled while the input is active (1). I've attached my program.
Thank you; it's much simpler once you know how! Is there a way to display 'In summer mode' when the input is active?
Yes, but could you clarify what the input represents: Is input '1' summer or is input '1' winter?
Thanks, it's working perfectly. You're fantastic, [user_name]. Now I'm looking for an M-bus to Modbus converter to utilize my water meter. After that, the project will be complete.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter difficulty when trying to implement control functions on the [product_name], including mode switching, output management, and integration of flow and water meters. Limited protocol support—such as no native M-Bus connectivity—and minimal built-in features for seasonal time management force users to rely on manual configuration or external solutions. The learning curve and lack of comprehensive beginner-friendly options reveal gaps in usability for users with limited technical experience.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope that [product_name] will allow flexible integration of inputs, automate seasonal switching with minimal manual involvement, and easily connect with external meters like those using M-Bus. Clear and practical guidance tailored for beginners is also sought.
